title: NOT A DEFECT: the scaffolding test invokes the pruned v2 intent_claude_upgrade; v3 writes .claude/settings.json correctly from the template
body:
A scaffolded project has no `.claude/settings.json`, though the template exists.

**Found by** `tests/unit/no_absolute_home_paths.bats` t5 ("a scaffolded project's hooks are portable and actually run") while establishing the causes of AC-06.1's 27 UNSTABLE files.

**Measured:** the assertion `[ -f .claude/settings.json ]` fails after scaffolding. `lib/templates/.claude/settings.json` is present in the tree, so the source of the file exists and something between the template and the scaffolded project does not deliver it.

**ROOT CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT GUESSED.** This issue records the observed failure and its control, nothing more.

**CONTROL:** `burn-baseline.tsv` records this file at DEFAULT_FAIL 0 on 2026-08-15, so it was green then and this is a regression inside that window. Note the file had 10 tests at the baseline and has 7 now, so the file itself changed; the control establishes that its default run was green, not that this particular test existed unchanged throughout.

**This file is MIXED.** Its other failure IS the AC-12.1 prune (a grep against the deleted `intent_claude_upgrade`). Only t5 is this issue. Recorded explicitly because a file with two causes is exactly where a single-cause attribution goes wrong.

**Relevance beyond the test:** `.claude/settings.json` is what wires the Claude Code session hooks. If scaffolding genuinely does not deliver it, new projects get no hooks and nothing reports that -- the failure is silent by construction.


=== NOT A DEFECT. THIS IS THE PRUNE, AND MY OWN SPLIT OF THE FILE WAS WRONG (cc, 2026-09-01) ===

**Driven, v2 entry point:**

    $ yes | bin/intent claude upgrade --apply
    error: Plugin command not found: intent/plugins/claude/bin/intent_claude_upgrade
    $ [ -f .claude/settings.json ] -> NO

**Driven, v3, the control:**

    $ yes | native/rust/target/release/intent claude upgrade --apply
    written: .claude/settings.json
    written: AGENTS.md
    written: usage-rules.md
    $ [ -f .claude/settings.json ] -> YES, 769 bytes, BYTE-IDENTICAL to lib/templates/.claude/settings.json

**So nothing is broken.** `intent_claude_upgrade` is one of the five v2 plugin scripts `125f601d` (AC-12.1's cutover prune) deleted. The test invokes the dead v2 entry point, gets `Plugin command not found`, and therefore nothing writes the file. **v3 writes it correctly, from the very template this issue cited as evidence that something was failing to deliver it.** The template was never the problem; the DELIVERER the test invokes was deleted on purpose.

**MY FILING WAS BUILT ON A SPLIT I DID NOT DRIVE.** `no_absolute_home_paths.bats` fails twice. I attributed t4 to the prune (it greps for the deleted file) and t5 to a separate unknown defect -- reasoning that t5's assertion was about a missing artefact rather than a missing command, without checking what the line ABOVE it invoked. **It invokes `claude upgrade`.** Both failures are one cause. I recorded the file as MIXED IN CAUSE on that split, on this issue and in `lib_classify.sh`'s OVERRIDES row, and both were wrong.

**This is the same error that produced this session's other two: taking the mechanism from an adjacent fact rather than from the thing itself.** Here the adjacent fact was the assertion that failed; the thing itself was the command two lines earlier.

**CONSEQUENCES, so nothing inherits the mistake:**

- `no_absolute_home_paths.bats` is WHOLLY prune-caused. Its OVERRIDES note is corrected; the MIXED IN CAUSE clause is struck.
- `AC-06.1`'s read has THREE causes that are not the prune, not four: `config.bats` t7 (`0200`) and `intent_critic.bats` t19 (`0201`) are real and separate; this is not.
- `AC-06.3`'s discharge cited three filings. It stands -- the row demands a recorded deviation or a filed defect and never silence, and reclassifying a filing after driving it is the opposite of silence -- but the count is two live defects plus this correction.

**CLOSED as not-a-defect.** The behaviour it describes is correct and deliberate, and the row it lives under is a `deviate` citing D10 like the other twenty-four.
